issues.title: [E] E1: ExecBackend interface + subprocess backend
issues.body:
deferred: after P1–P2 are done (Felix, 10.11.)

**Problem**

Coding agents need a single, honest execution interface. Today there is no shared `ExecBackend`: isolation is implicit, can be silently weaker than requested, and must not depend on klanker or calendar. Architecture proposal only (Felix 20:49, Track E).

**Target state**

`ExecBackend` interface + a stdlib-only subprocess backend, in agents-harness.

- Stdlib only for this card (no Docker/Podman/bwrap/nsjail extras here; those are E2).
- Auto-detect with a fallback chain.
- `cwd` = workdir.
- Reports `isolation_level` honestly: `container` | `os-sandbox` | `process` | `remote`. The reported level is never upgraded.
- `min_isolation` -> error if unmet; never a silent downgrade.
- Interface includes network, mounts, and an env allowlist.
- Secrets never in the workdir.
- Windows/macOS report `process`.
- The chosen level is written to traces.
- No dependency on klanker or calendar.
- Interface stays. Work is deferred until after P1–P2 are done (Felix, 10.11.).

**Steps (architecture)**

- Specify the interface (methods, `isolation_level`, `min_isolation`, network/mounts/env-allowlist).
- Specify the stdlib subprocess backend and the auto-detect / fallback chain.
- Specify how the level is recorded in traces.
- Implementation follows only after P1–P2 are done and Felix has not changed the Track E defaults.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Interface and subprocess backend match the target (proposal accepted).
- [ ] Reported `isolation_level` is honest and never upgraded; `min_isolation` errors instead of silently downgrading.
- [ ] Secrets are not written into the workdir; Windows/macOS report `process`; level is in traces.
- [ ] No import/dependency on klanker or calendar.

**Depends on**

none (can start now; no P1 dependency)

issues.title: [Bug] a2a.peer: env-blind relay URL (hardcoded 8787, ignores RELAY_PORT) + fake ok:true stub on failure
issues.body:
**Problem**

1. `a2a.peer` (`runner/modules/a2a.peer.json`, `POST /v1/a2a/mail`) hardcodes `GATEWAY_URL` default `http://127.0.0.1:8787` and ignores `RELAY_URL`/`RELAY_PORT`. On-host this happens to match the relay default (`RELAY_PORT` default 8787, `agents_relay/config.py`), but inside the klanker container the image sets `RELAY_PORT=8000` (`klanker/Dockerfile`), so the module hits connection refused (`Errno 111`). Resolution must follow the same env chain as the relay (`RELAY_URL` / `RELAY_PORT`, `GATEWAY_*` only as deprecated fallback).
2. On connection/transport failure, `a2a.peer` currently returns `{"ok": true, "stub": true}`, which causes the harness tool receipt to record success even though nothing was delivered.
3. Contract ambiguity: `a2a.peer` is confused with intra-workspace persona communication when in reality it proxies cross-host / `agents-board` DID mail (`/v1/a2a/mail`).

**Scope**
- Resolve target URL from `RELAY_URL` (else `http://127.0.0.1:$RELAY_PORT`, else `GATEWAY_URL` fallback) so the module works on-host (8787) and in-container (8000) without hardcoding.
- Return `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` and non-zero exit code on transport failure so tool receipts never report false delivery.
- Clarify module description/schema that `a2a.peer` is for cross-host board DID mail, while intra-workspace persona communication uses `persona.*`.

**Acceptance**
- Calling `a2a.peer` with an unreachable URL exits non-zero with `ok: false` and no `stub: true`.
- Unit tests cover connection error handling and explicit URL env resolution.

issues.title: [Feature] Cordis persona.* modules (list, inbox, ask, handoff) + unspoofable sender & loop guardrails
issues.body:
**Goal**

Give LLM turns native Cordis tools (`runner/modules/`) to discover sibling personas in the same workspace, inspect their inbox, ask quick 1-turn questions synchronously, and trigger async handoffs — following strict Cordis layering (CLI calls via `klanker persona ...`, no importing `klanker` or `agents_workspace` internals).

**Modules (`runner/modules/`)**
- `persona.list` (read-only): list workspace personas (`id`, `name`, `role`, `accepts_messages`) via `klanker persona list --json`.
- `persona.inbox` (read-only): read open/recent inbox tasks for current or named persona.
- `persona.ask` (side-effect/controlled): synchronous 1-turn consultation (`klanker persona ask <to> "<prompt>"`) — returns target persona's reply directly into the tool result, tagged with `thread_id`.
- `persona.handoff` (mutating): create/transfer task in `agents_workspace.inbox` and optionally pass `--wake`.

**Guardrails**
- Unspoofable sender identity: `from_persona` comes from `AGENTS_PERSONA`, never trusted from model JSON args.
- Loop protection: propagate `AGENTS_PERSONA_HOP`; refuse calls when `hop >= max_hops` (default `3`) or direct self-loop without explicit override.
- `help-json` metadata: mark `persona.list` and `persona.inbox` as `read-only` so approval mode handles them cleanly.

**Related**
- Depends on workspace schema: https://board.lolaplex.org/projects/agents-workspace/issues/17
- Coordinate `persona.json` allowlist with `agents-harness#12`.

**Acceptance**
- `python -m runner.executor --validate` passes with new `persona.*` manifests.
- Harness unit test verifies `AGENTS_PERSONA_HOP` cap stops recursive persona ping-pong at `max_hops`.

issues.title: cordis: one module per suite package via help-json
issues.body:
Cordis discovery phase 1 — replace hand-written subcommand manifests with live help-json discovery.

Today `mcp.memory`, `mcp.traces`, `mcp.browser` are presence probes only; real tools are per-subcommand manifests (`mcp.memory.add`, `mcp.memory.read`, `mcp.memory.search`, `mcp.memory.projects`, `mcp.traces.audit`, `mcp.traces.seal`, `mcp.calendar.*`) plus arg-mapping shims in `runner/cordis_tools.py`. The CLIs already emit full help-json (agents-memory ~40 commands).

Plan:
- `commands_from: "help-json"` + `as_tool` on the package modules; commands/params/side-effects come live from the CLI.
- Deprecate subcommand manifests and their cordis_tools shim cases once discovery covers them.
- Optional `"expose_commands": [...]` manifest key to split selected commands into their own tools (better tool choice + toolset granularity) — same help-json source.

Done with mcp.model + mcp.delegate on feat/model-switch and feat/delegate-task (declared commands, shims removed) — use as reference.

Blocked: mcp.memory until the agents-memory rework (cypoe) lands.

issues.title: cordis: subcommand-level side-effect classes in help-json
issues.body:
Cordis discovery phase 2 — one more level of command depth in help-json classification.

Today `select_command`/`call_effects` classify on argv[0] only: `proc` is one mutating command even though `proc list|poll|log` are read-only and `proc write|kill` are mutating. Same for any `verb action` CLI (schedule, delegate, memory).

Plan:
- Extend the help-json command spec with a `subcommands` object (one level) carrying usage/parameters/side_effects per action.
- Resolve two levels in `runner/helpjson.py` (`argv[0]`+`argv[1]`, or an `action` argument key) for `select_command`, `declared_argv`, `call_effects`, and pinned rendering.
- Emitters: agents-terminal `proc`, runner.delegate, runner.model, agents-calendar — emit nested specs.

Result: approval classes per action (`proc poll` ungated, `proc kill` gated) without new modules.

issues.title: cordis: auto-mount suite packages (cordis_expose) + toolset mapping
issues.body:
Cordis discovery phase 3 — install-time tool discovery instead of checked-in manifests.

Dream-state: installing an agents-* package exposes its commands as Cordis tools without a module JSON in this repo.

Plan:
- `cordis_expose: true` convention in a package's `--help-json` output (plus optional `group` tags per command).
- `runner.modules` scans installed suite packages and synthesizes module manifests at runtime (same shape as files; overlays still win).
- `klanker sense` shows discovered-but-unmounted capabilities with an enable flow.
- Toolsets (#22 follow-up) get a natural mapping: toolset name = package name, groups from command metadata.

Keep Cordis rules: executor still only runs CLIs and reads exit codes; fail-closed classification stays (missing side_effects = mutating).

issues.title: Persona memory split: private|shared flag in persona.json
issues.body: Today: sessions are per-persona (<ws>/personas/<id>/sessions/) but memory is fully ws-shared; only notes.md is persona-private. Grokbot-style model needs per-persona memory + shared ws memory. Minimal path: persona.json flag "memory": "private" resolves memory root to <ws>/personas/<id>/memory/ instead of ws.memory for that persona's turns; "shared" (default) keeps current behaviour. Retrieval surfaces shared memory + persona memory (private only for that persona). Depends on nothing; complements agents-memory#15 (retrieval at scale).

issues.title: Delegate depth ledger: replace env-only counter
issues.body: feat/delegate-task hardened recursion with AGENTS_DELEGATE_DEPTH env counter - strippable via env -u by a delegate that spawns its own delegate. Best-effort fix without kernel boundary: depth ledger file <ws>/run/delegate.depth written by parent before spawn (host-side, not env-inherited), child reads and increments; refuse beyond MAX. Still same-uid advisory but kills the trivial env-strip path. Real isolation stays the container card (agents-workspace). Lands as follow-up after delegate-task merges.

decided (Klanker, technical, 10.11.): D-mcp-level — <host>/mcp.json + optional <ws>/mcp.json overlay
decided (Klanker, technical, 10.11.): D-config — <host>/agents.json
decided (Klanker, technical, 10.11.): D-file-suffix — AGENTS_IDENTITY_PATH->AGENTS_USERS_FILE (points to <host>/users.json), AGENTS_KNOWN_DIDS->AGENTS_KNOWN_DIDS_FILE, AGENTS_MCP_CONFIG->AGENTS_MCP_CONFIG_FILE, AGENTS_MCP_CACHE->AGENTS_MCP_CACHE_FILE, AGENTS_SYNC_CONFIG->AGENTS_SYNC_CONFIG_FILE (alias 1 release each)

**Problem**

issues.title: [P2] Load personas from <ws>/personas/<id> (package personas as fallback); AGENTS_PERSONA id
issues.body:
decided (Felix 10.11. 19:31): D-persona-default (P2) — Personas are equal, no hierarchy; a role (e.g. CoS) is a persona with a role description. First persona 'default' is created with the workspace. Explicit handoffs: inbox per persona + clear task ownership. decided (Felix 10.11. 19:31): Workspace memory is shared by all its personas; a persona may have optional private notes. **Problem** QA Phase 2: `personas/` is only a path; `workspace.json` stores `default_persona` (`workspace.py:89, 277-284`); `env()` exports `AGENTS_PERSONAS_DIR` and no persona id. Inventory: `runner/personas.py:8` `PERSONAS_DIR` = package dir only (`AGENTS_PERSONAS_DIR` set, never read); `loop.py:650` `--persona` from the package. **Target state** `/personas//persona.json` first, package personas as fallback; `--persona ` / `AGENTS_PERSONA`. Personas are equal (no hierarchy); a role (e.g. CoS) is a persona with a role description, not a higher layer. First persona `default` is created with the workspace (renamable, no special role) — do not treat `workspace.json default_persona` as a hidden default-persona hierarchy (D-persona-default, decided Felix 10.11. 19:31). Workspace memory is shared; a persona may have optional private notes.
